title: Outcomes of a Process: terminar por and acabar por

sections.content:
You know *terminar por* and *acabar por* + infinitive from B2 Unit 25. In economic columns, these periphrases describe how prolonged pressure, debate or hesitation eventually resolves into a policy decision or a market outcome.

Both *terminar por* and *acabar por* take a bare infinitive and can appear in any tense (*acabó por subir*, *terminará por frenar*, *han acabado por afectar*). They signal that the outcome came at the end of a chain of events rather than abruptly out of nowhere.

sections.title: terminar por / acabar por in economic narrative
rows: Preterite: El banco central acabó por subir las tasas de interés.
The central bank ended up raising interest rates.
Present perfect: Los aranceles han terminado por encarecer las importaciones.
The tariffs have ended up making imports more expensive.
Future: La falta de inversión terminará por frenar la producción.
The lack of investment will end up slowing production.

items.spanish: Tras meses de debate, el comité acabó por aprobar el ajuste.
items.english: After months of debate, the committee ended up approving the adjustment.

items.spanish: El deterioro del crédito terminó por enfriar la demanda interna.
items.english: The deterioration of credit ended up cooling domestic demand.

items.spanish: Un arancel demasiado alto acaba por perjudicar al propio consumidor.
items.english: An overly high tariff ends up harming the consumer as well.

sections.content: Watch the preposition: *acabar de* + infinitive (A2 Unit 32) means 'to have just done', whereas *acabar por* + infinitive means 'to end up doing'. Never drop *por* before the infinitive, and use these periphrases only when a prior process leads to the outcome.
